Test sedimentation rates with noise-corrected TimeOpt, likelihood and COCO scores

Source: R/astro_sedrate_test.R
astro_sedrate_test.Rd

Scans a grid of constant sedimentation rates for one stratigraphic record and scores every rate in three ways: the TimeOpt envelope and spectral fits (Meyers, 2015), a likelihood-based evidence score with an information-criterion penalty (in the spirit of Malinverno and Meyers, 2024) and the COCO correlation coefficient (Li et al., 2018). Every score is expressed against noise analysed at the same rate, rates that cannot be tested are masked, astronomical target periods can be taken at the age of the record from AstroGeo22 (Farhat et al., 2022), the TimeOpt and COCO scores are combined into one score, and the result is repeated for several noise models.

Usage

astro_sedrate_test(
  data = NULL,
  sedmin = 1,
  sedmax = 20,
  numsed = 100,
  linLog = 1,
  fit = 1,
  age_ma = NULL,
  targetE = NULL,
  targetP = NULL,
  targetO = NULL,
  obliquity = TRUE,
  fitModPwr = TRUE,
  ftol = NULL,
  roll = 10^7,
  detrend = TRUE,
  penalty = c("BIC", "AIC"),
  coco = TRUE,
  combine = c("timeopt_coco", "all"),
  noise_model = c("auto", "ar1", "ar2", "powerlaw", "bending"),
  null_fit = c("local", "masked", "full"),
  mask_pad = 2,
  local_factor = 4,
  tune = c("none", "minimal"),
  tune_width = 0.3,
  tune_fit_tuned = FALSE,
  band_guard = TRUE,
  obliquity_mod = TRUE,
  edge_trim = "auto",
  tuned_peaks = TRUE,
  peak_tol = 0.05,
  keep_null = FALSE,
  sensitivity = TRUE,
  target_sensitivity = TRUE,
  n_null = 200,
  null_smooth = 2,
  alpha = 0.05,
  min_samples = 3,
  min_cycles = 2,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Evenly spaced stratigraphic record (matrix or data frame with two columns: depth in metres in column 1, proxy value in column 2; further columns are ignored). The rows are sorted by depth; the record is detrended (see detrend) and standardised before the analysis. Required, no default (Default=NULL gives an error).

sedmin, sedmax

Lowest and highest trial sedimentation rate of the rate grid, in cm/kyr (numeric, > 0, sedmin < sedmax). Default=1 and Default=20.

numsed

Number of trial sedimentation rates in the grid (integer, >= 1; 1 tests sedmin only). Default=100.

linLog

Spacing of the rate grid (numeric): 1 logarithmic, 0 linear. Default=1.

fit

Which TimeOpt fit is used (numeric): 1 precession carrier modulated by eccentricity, 2 short-eccentricity carrier modulated by the 405-kyr eccentricity. Default=1.

age_ma

Age of the record in Ma (numeric, 0 to 4429), used to compute the precession and obliquity target periods from the AstroGeo22 precession frequency (astrogeo22); NULL uses the present-day precession frequency. Values given in targetE, targetP or targetO override the computed periods. Default=NULL.

targetE, targetP, targetO

Your own eccentricity, precession and obliquity target periods in kyr (numeric vectors, any order; they are sorted from longest to shortest). For fit = 2 the longest value of targetE is the modulating (405-kyr) period and the others are the carrier periods. NULL uses the La2004/AstroGeo22 periods (see age_ma). Default=NULL.

obliquity

Include the obliquity periods in the spectral (power) fit and in the COCO target (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

fitModPwr

Include the modulating eccentricity periods in the spectral (power) fit (logical, TRUE or FALSE), as in astrochron::timeOpt. Default=TRUE.

ftol

Half-width added outside the carrier frequencies to define the Taner bandpass, in cycles/kyr (numeric, >= 0); NULL uses 0.005 for the precession carrier (fit 1) and 0.001 for the short-eccentricity carrier (fit 2). Default=NULL.

roll

Roll-off rate of the Taner bandpass filter used for the carrier band (numeric, > 0; see astrochron::taner). Default=10^7.

detrend

Remove a linear trend from the proxy before the analysis (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

penalty

Information-criterion penalty of the likelihood score (character): "BIC" (k log N) or "AIC" (2k). Default=c("BIC", "AIC"), i.e. "BIC".

coco

Compute the COCO correlation score (and the scores that combine it) (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

combine

Which scores enter the combined scores z_comb and z_cons (character): "timeopt_coco" (TimeOpt and COCO) or "all" (TimeOpt, COCO and the likelihood score). Default=c("timeopt_coco", "all"), i.e. "timeopt_coco".

noise_model

Noise model of the null series (character): "auto" (the model with the lowest AIC), "ar1", "ar2", "powerlaw" or "bending" (bending power law). With sensitivity = TRUE the other models are also run, but the main result uses this one. Default=c("auto", "ar1", "ar2", "powerlaw", "bending"), i.e. "auto".

null_fit

How the noise model is fitted to the periodogram (character): "local" at every rate without the astronomical bands, near the tested frequencies and with its parameter uncertainty (see Details); "masked" at every rate without the bands but with all other frequencies; "full" once, to the whole periodogram. Default=c("local", "masked", "full"), i.e. "local".

mask_pad

Widening of every masked astronomical band on each side, in Rayleigh frequencies (1 / duration) (numeric, >= 0); used when null_fit is "local" or "masked". Default=2.

local_factor

Upper frequency limit of the "local" noise fit, in multiples of the highest target frequency of the spectral fit (numeric, > 1; at least 40 frequencies are always used). Default=4.

tune

Tuning applied at every trial rate before scoring (character): "none" (constant rate) or "minimal" (tune with the 405-kyr cycle for fit 2, the short eccentricity for fit 1; see Details). Default=c("none", "minimal"), i.e. "none".

tune_width

Relative half-width of the bandpass around the period predicted by the trial rate that extracts the tuning cycle (numeric, between 0 and 1; also the allowed deviation of the local rate); used by tune = "minimal" and by the tuned-band peak score. Default=0.3.

tune_fit_tuned

Keep the tuned cycle in the spectral fit after minimal tuning (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE leaves it out because the tuning imposes its regularity. Default=FALSE.

band_guard

Keep every other astronomical term out of the carrier bandpass (logical, TRUE or FALSE): each band edge is moved at most halfway to the nearest term outside the carrier set (for fit 2 the ~151-kyr s4-s6 obliquity-modulation term next to the 131-kyr short eccentricity). Default=TRUE.

obliquity_mod

Include the obliquity-modulation terms s3-s6 (~173 kyr) and s4-s6 (~151 kyr) in the spectral fit (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

edge_trim

Time in kyr removed at both ends of the envelope before the envelope fit (numeric, >= 0, or the character "auto"): "auto" removes one impulse length of the carrier filter (1 / bandwidth), 0 removes nothing (as astrochron::timeOpt). Default="auto".

tuned_peaks

Compute the tuned-band peak score S_peaks and the joint score S_joint (see Details) (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=TRUE.

peak_tol

Relative tolerance around each tested period in the tuned-band peak score (numeric, > 0; 0.05 = periods within 5% of the target). Default=0.05.

keep_null

Return the same-rate p of every noise series (matrix rates x noise series) for S_opt, S_peaks and S_joint in null_p, as needed by astro_sedrate_multi (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

sensitivity

Repeat the test for all four noise models and report them in sensitivity (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE runs only the chosen model, which is faster. Default=TRUE.

target_sensitivity

Repeat the scores with the AstroGeo22 minimum and maximum precession frequency (logical, TRUE or FALSE; only used when age_ma is given). Default=TRUE.

n_null

Number of noise series simulated per noise model (integer, > 0); the smallest family-wise probability that can be reached is 1/(n_null + 1). Default=200.

null_smooth

Half-width in grid steps of the smoothing of the noise mean and standard deviation over neighbouring rates, and of the pooling of the noise series of neighbouring rates for S_opt (integer, >= 0). Default=2.

alpha

False-alarm level (numeric, between 0 and 1); stored in the settings of the result. Default=0.05.

min_samples

Minimum number of samples per shortest carrier period; rates with fewer are marked untestable (code 1) (numeric, > 0). Default=3.

min_cycles

Minimum number of cycles of the longest modulating period that the record must span at a rate; rates with fewer are marked untestable (code 2) (numeric, > 0). Default=2.

run_multicore

Simulate and score the noise series in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores used for the noise series (integer); NULL uses the option waverider.n_cores or, with run_multicore = TRUE, all but one detected core (at most getOption("waverider.max_cores", 4)). Default=NULL.

verbose

Print progress messages (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

Value

A list of class astro_sedrate_test with

scores

data frame per rate: sedrate, untestable code, r2_envelope, r2_power, r2_opt, z_envelope, z_power, z_opt, p_opt, B_spectral, B_envelope, B_total, weight_lik, z_lik, p_lik, coco_rho, z_coco, p_coco, z_comb, p_comb, z_cons, p_cons, S_opt, p_S, S_peaks, p_peaks, S_joint, p_joint (p = family-wise probability; S = -log10 of the same-rate p)

best

data frame: best rate, value and family-wise p of each score (raw r2_opt included)

null_p

with keep_null = TRUE: same-rate p of every noise series (rates x noise series) for S_opt, S_peaks and S_joint; otherwise NULL

significance_levels

matrix (rows TimeOpt, peaks, joint): S values of the family-wise 5 % and 1 % levels

tuning

for tune = "minimal": depth, time (kyr), sedimentation rate (cm/kyr) and tie points of the minimal-tuning age model at the rate selected by S_opt

corroboration

value and family-wise p of every score at the rate selected by S_opt, and the ratio of each score's own best rate to that rate (to spot aliases)

sensitivity

best rate, z and p of every score for every noise model

target_sensitivity

best rates with the AstroGeo22 minimum / nominal / maximum precession frequency

noise_fits

fitted noise models with their AIC (summed over the testable rates for null_fit = "local" or "masked")

noise_fits_rate

for null_fit = "local" or "masked": AIC and parameters of every noise model at every testable rate, and the fraction of periodogram frequencies kept

targets

the target periods used

settings

the settings

Details

Why a same-rate noise correction. The raw TimeOpt r-squared values (and COCO correlations) that pure noise reaches depend on the trial rate: at high rates the record spans a short time, fewer cycles fit, and the regression has fewer independent data points per fitted sinusoid; for red noise the target frequencies also move to the strong low-frequency end of the spectrum. Li et al. (2018) describe the same effect for COCO (fewer astronomical terms resolved at high rates). Here every statistic is compared with the same statistic of noise series analysed at the same rate: $$z(u) = (S(u) - \mu_{noise}(u)) / \sigma_{noise}(u)$$ (r-squared values on a logit scale, COCO correlations on a Fisher z scale; the noise mean and standard deviation are smoothed over neighbouring rates). The family-wise probability of a score is the fraction of noise series whose maximum z over all testable rates is at least as large (as in the full-grid test of Meyers and Malinverno, 2018), with a floor of 1/(n_null + 1).

TimeOpt scores. For each rate the record is calibrated to time, the carrier band (precession for fit 1, short eccentricity for fit 2) is bandpassed with taner, its amplitude envelope is taken with hilbert and regressed on the modulating periods (eccentricity for fit 1, the 405-kyr term for fit 2), and the record itself is regressed on the target periods. r2_envelope, r2_power and r2_opt follow Meyers (2015); z_opt combines the z-scores of the envelope and power fits (Stouffer's method).

Significance spectrum (main TimeOpt score). S_opt refers the envelope and the power fit each to the noise distribution at the same rate (the noise series of that rate and of the null_smooth neighbouring rates pooled; an exponential tail above the pooled 75 % quantile resolves p below 1 / n_null), combines the two p-values (Fisher) and calibrates the combination the same way; S_opt = -log10 of that p. The family-wise p (p_S) uses the minimum-p method (Westfall and Young, 1993): the share of noise series whose smallest p over the testable rates is at least as small. Because every rate is referred to its own noise distribution, noise gives a flat baseline near zero over the whole range (no drift to fast rates as in raw r2_opt, and no inflated low-rate scatter as in z_opt), and the family-wise levels are horizontal lines.

Tuned-band peaks and joint score. TimeOpt's envelope fit has little power when the record spans few modulating cycles and the rate changes (in a Kosov-like test, about 2 Myr with +-17 % rate changes, the fit-2 envelope reached p < 0.05 at the true rate in 15-30 % of records with a known signal). With tuned_peaks = TRUE a second score is computed at every rate: the record is minimally tuned on the 405-kyr cycle (fit 2) or on the short eccentricity (fit 1) at that rate (as tune = "minimal"), and the bands not used for the tuning (short eccentricity, obliquity, precession for fit 2; obliquity and precession for fit 1) are tested for spectral peaks: the mean over these bands of the largest log ratio of the periodogram to a smooth continuum (cubic in log frequency fitted to the log periodogram with the peaks left out) within peak_tol of each period. Every noise series is tuned and scored in exactly the same way, so the regularity that the tuning imposes is part of the null and the test is not circular; the tuned band itself is not scored. S_peaks is -log10 of the same-rate p with the minimum-p family-wise p_peaks, as for S_opt. In the Kosov-like test this score reached p < 0.05 in 90-100 % of records with a known signal. S_joint combines S_opt and S_peaks (Fisher) and is calibrated again on the same noise series (p_joint); use it as the main summary when both are available.

Likelihood score. This score is complementary to TimeOpt and follows ideas of timeOptB (Malinverno and Meyers, 2024): the residuals of the spectral fit are modelled as an AR(2) process (the likelihood is that of the AR(2) innovations), and the envelope fit uses an effective number of independent points N_eff = N / tau, with tau the first lag at which the autocorrelation of the envelope reaches zero. At every rate the astronomical model is compared with a model without astronomical terms, and an information-criterion penalty is applied for the number of resolvable terms: $$B = 2 (\log L_{astro} - \log L_{noise}) - k \log N$$ (BIC, penalty = "BIC") or \(- 2k\) (AIC). Only target terms that the record can resolve at that rate enter the likelihood model: terms with fewer than min_samples samples per cycle or with periods longer than the record are dropped, and terms closer in frequency than the Rayleigh resolution (1 / duration) are merged into one. B > 0 means the astronomical model is preferred at that rate; weight_lik gives rate weights proportional to exp(B / 2). The likelihood score is a model comparison per rate, not a full Bayesian posterior: the envelope differs between rates, so the weights are indicative. Use timeOptB for posterior distributions of the sedimentation rate and the precession frequency.

COCO. The correlation coefficient between the AR(1)-corrected periodogram of the record and an astronomical target periodogram (coco_classic, coco_target_from_periods; Li et al., 2018).

Combined scores. z_comb is the sum of z_opt and z_coco, standardised again against the same noise series, so the correlation between the TimeOpt and COCO scores is accounted for. z_cons (consensus) is the smaller of the two z-scores, standardised in the same way: it is only high where both methods support the rate, which suppresses peaks that only one method shows (e.g. the COCO alias at ~4.3 times the true rate, where eccentricity cycles are read as precession and short eccentricity). With combine = "all" the likelihood score is added to both.

Noise models. AR(1), AR(2), power law (f^-beta) and bending power law (1 / (1 + (f / f_b)^beta); Vaughan et al., 2011), fitted to the periodogram of the record (Whittle likelihood). noise_model = "auto" uses the model with the lowest AIC. sensitivity = TRUE repeats the test for every noise model.

Noise fitted without the cycles (null_fit). A noise model fitted to the whole periodogram of the record also fits the astronomical cycles in it, and its shape near the tested frequencies is set mainly by the many high-frequency periodogram values. Both distort the background at the frequencies that matter: cycles that are present bend the fitted spectrum (e.g. an AR(1) background is fitted as AR(2)), so the null partly contains the cycles it is tested against and genuine cycles look less significant. Therefore, by default (null_fit = "local"), the noise model is fitted separately for every trial rate (Whittle likelihood):

  • leaving out the frequency bands where that rate puts the astronomical terms (405-kyr eccentricity, short eccentricity, obliquity and precession, each band widened by mask_pad Rayleigh frequencies 1 / duration), as in robust background estimates that exclude spectral peaks (Mann and Lees, 1996; Meyers, 2012);

  • using only frequencies up to local_factor times the highest target frequency of the spectral fit (at least 40 frequencies), so the background is estimated where the tested cycles are;

  • carrying the uncertainty of the fitted parameters (Whittle Hessian) into the noise series: every noise series draws its parameters from that uncertainty, so a background that is poorly constrained by few frequencies gives a wider null instead of false alarms.

The noise series for a rate come from the model fitted at that rate; the same random numbers are used at all rates, so each noise series is one coherent "noise world" over the rate grid and the family-wise probability keeps its meaning. The model choice (noise_model = "auto") uses the AIC summed over the testable rates. null_fit = "masked" leaves out the bands but uses all other frequencies; null_fit = "full" fits one noise model to the whole periodogram (earlier behaviour).

Minimal tuning (tune = "minimal"). A constant trial rate smears the cycles when the true rate varies, so the TimeOpt fit can favour a wrong rate. With minimal tuning the record is first tuned at every trial (mean) rate with the highest-order cycle only: for fit 2 the 405-kyr cycle, for fit 1 the short eccentricity (tied at the harmonic mean of its periods, ~110 kyr). The cycle is bandpassed in depth around the period the trial rate predicts (+- tune_width), every cycle of its (monotonic) Hilbert phase is tied to the cycle period, time is interpolated linearly between the ties and extrapolated at the trial rate beyond them, and TimeOpt, the likelihood score and COCO are computed on the tuned series. The tuned cycle is left out of the spectral fit (tune_fit_tuned = FALSE) because the tuning imposes its regularity. Every noise series is tuned in exactly the same way at every rate, so the gain in fit that tuning gives to any series is part of the null and the probabilities stay calibrated. tuning returns the minimal-tuning age model at the rate selected by z_opt. The trial rate is then the mean rate of a tuned age model, so the test asks at which scale a 405-kyr (or short-eccentricity) tuning gives the best astronomical fit.

Envelope and band corrections (fit 2). Three settings protect the modulation fit of TimeOpt (fit 2 in particular) against artefacts found on real records:

  • edge_trim: the Taner bandpass and the Hilbert transform ring at the ends of a finite record, and the ringing extends over about one impulse length of the filter (1 / bandwidth, ~230 kyr for the short-eccentricity band). With only a few 405-kyr cycles these end values steer the envelope regression; they are removed before the fit (and from the duration used for the untestable mask).

  • band_guard: the default fit-2 band (1/130.7 - 0.001 to 1/94.9 + 0.001 cycles/kyr, i.e. 87-151 kyr) contains the s4-s6 obliquity-modulation term (151 kyr); the long-period edge is moved halfway to it (~140 kyr).

  • obliquity_mod: the s3-s6 and s4-s6 terms are part of the spectral model, so their power counts at the rate where they belong. Otherwise a rate ~1.2-1.3 times too high, at which the short-eccentricity targets fall on the obliquity-modulation cycles, can win.

With band_guard = FALSE, obliquity_mod = FALSE, edge_trim = 0 the r-squared values are those of astrochron::timeOpt.

Age-dependent targets. With age_ma, the target periods are computed from the AstroGeo22 precession frequency (Farhat et al., 2022; astrogeo22) and the La2004 secular frequencies (Laskar et al., 2004; held at their present values): eccentricity g2-g5, g3-g2, g4-g2, g3-g5, g4-g5; precession k+g5, k+g2, k+g4, k+g3; obliquity k+s3, k+s4, k+s6. target_sensitivity = TRUE repeats the scores with the AstroGeo22 minimum and maximum precession frequency.

Untestable rates (untestable): 1 = fewer than min_samples samples per shortest carrier period; 2 = the record spans fewer than min_cycles of the longest modulating period.

References

Meyers, S.R. (2015). The evaluation of eccentricity-related amplitude modulation and bundling in paleoclimate data: An inverse approach for astrochronologic testing and time scale optimization. Paleoceanography 30, 1625-1640 <doi:10.1002/2015PA002850>

Westfall, P.H. and Young, S.S. (1993). Resampling-Based Multiple Testing: Examples and Methods for p-Value Adjustment. Wiley, New York, ISBN 978-0-471-55761-6.

Meyers, S.R. and Malinverno, A. (2018). Proterozoic Milankovitch cycles and the history of the solar system. PNAS 115, 6363-6368 <doi:10.1073/pnas.1717689115>

Malinverno, A. and Meyers, S.R. (2024). Bayesian estimation of past astronomical frequencies, lunar distance, and length of day from sediment cycles. Geochemistry, Geophysics, Geosystems 25, e2023GC011176 <doi:10.1029/2023GC011176>

Li, M., Kump, L.R., Hinnov, L.A. and Mann, M.E. (2018). Tracking variable sedimentation rates and astronomical forcing in Phanerozoic paleoclimate proxy series with evolutionary correlation coefficients and hypothesis testing. Earth and Planetary Science Letters 501, 165-179 <doi:10.1016/j.epsl.2018.08.041>

Farhat, M., Auclair-Desrotour, P., Boue, G. and Laskar, J. (2022). The resonant tidal evolution of the Earth-Moon distance. Astronomy and Astrophysics 665, L1 <doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202243445>

Mann, M.E. and Lees, J.M. (1996). Robust estimation of background noise and signal detection in climatic time series. Climatic Change 33, 409-445 <doi:10.1007/BF00142586>

Meyers, S.R. (2012). Seeing red in cyclic stratigraphy: Spectral noise estimation for astrochronology. Paleoceanography 27, PA3228 <doi:10.1029/2012PA002307>

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
res <- astro_sedrate_test(data = mag[1:400, ], sedmin = 0.3, sedmax = 1.5, numsed = 25,
    fit = 1, n_null = 10, sensitivity = FALSE, target_sensitivity = FALSE)
res$best
